page: Amazon Web Services r8g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 Arm-based Graviton processors on the Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 192 dedicated physical cores running 192 vCPUs at 2.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 1536.0 GB of memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include support for hardware AES cryptographic operations, alongside a cache topology of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per processor subsystem. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, zero dedicated public IPv4 addresses, and includes no local instance storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier performance in parallelized, multi-core computing and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng, the multi-core score reaches 314965.45, placing in the top 10%, while single-core performance remains in the middle 50% with a score of 1644.69. Similarly, Geekbench highlights this distinction, recording a multi-core score of 20740.0 in the top 10% alongside an average single-core score of 1659.0. Memory bandwidth results are in the top tier, measuring 1084.93 GB/sec on uncached 256MB reads and 494.91 GB/sec on writes. High-throughput server workloads demonstrate significant scale, with Redis SET operations achieving 363.6 million operations per second, PassMark database operations scoring 46777.01, and static web serving throughput reaching 174.24 GB/sec.

The qualitative hardware balance delivers high compute and memory capacity per server footprint, though workloads dependent on single-threaded frequency will find standard throughput. Architectural tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe storage, requiring reliance on networked block storage for persistent input and output, as well as the absence of hardware vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX. Large CPU-bound parallel workloads benefit from the dedicated 1:1 physical core execution model without thread contention.

Given its massive memory allocation, 50 Gbps network profile, and top-tier multi-threaded database benchmarks, AWS r8g.48xlarge fits large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, memory-intensive distributed caching layers, large enterprise database deployments, Clang compilation pipelines, and heavy ETL processing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance driven by 192-core AWS Neoverse-V2 arm64 processors operating at 2.7 GHz with dedicated physical cores and Nitro virtualization. Supplying 1536.0 GB of system memory at an 8:1 GB-per-core ratio, it includes 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance shows exceptional multi-core and memory capabilities, reaching top-decile ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing (314965.45), PassMark database operations (46777.01), uncached memory read bandwidth (1084.93 GB/sec), and Redis throughput (363.6 million ops/sec). Single-core metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench fall within median ranges, establishing it as an infrastructure choice tailored for concurrent, memory-heavy applications. The hardware architecture makes it optimal for large in-memory databases, memory-constrained data analysis, enterprise caching clusters, and extensive multi-threaded compilation workloads.
